- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to historical mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to prevent overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion — if price is deviating >2σ from 30-day moving average, forecast should align with recent sentiment-driven momentum, not pure technical reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price action; increase forecast by 1–4% for final 7–10 days if sentiment is rising or volatile.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 0.5 → 0.1 → 0.5), model misreads momentum; apply smoothing filter to sentiment before weighting in forecast.
